punchline: Medallion's famous 66 percent is an average, and an average is not compounding.
thirty_sec: Zuckerman reports Medallion averaged 66.1 percent a year before fees and 39.1 percent after, 1988 to 2018. Professor Bradford Cornell calculated that $100 would have become about $398.7 million. A 2024 paper argues the compounded return before fees was probably under 35 percent.
question: Which impressive figure that you quote at work or at home have you never checked for how it was calculated?
key_contrast: An average of yearly returns and a compounded growth rate answer different questions.
